summary: multipart stream: mid-stream credential rotation rewrites idempotency header and causes duplicate tool executions (Python client + Go webhook)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate downstream tool (webhook) executions when their long-running streaming session experiences an auth credential refresh. The idempotency/confirmation header added by the Python SDK is being rewritten/truncated during a mid-stream credential rotation at the API gateway which causes the server to treat the resumed chunk as a new request, re-invoking the tool webhook.

Context: QueryFlow uses the Redwood streaming chat endpoint with function/tool calling. Their Python client streams tokens and the server calls out to a customer-managed Go webhook to execute side effects. When the customer's token refreshes mid-stream (their environment rotates delegated credentials), we see duplicate webhook invocations in their logs.
impact: Customer reports repeated duplicate side-effects (duplicate invoice sends and duplicate database writes) for ~2% of long-running streaming sessions. Business impact: end-user confusion and extra downstream processing, customer unable to safely rely on at-most-once semantics for streaming tool calls. Affects production workloads on dedicated capacity in us-east.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Create a long-lived streaming chat session using Python SDK and enable function/tool calling to a test Go webhook that logs invocations.
2. Start a multi-chunk generation (simulate >30s stream) that triggers a funcall during streaming (e.g., user asks to submit a batch job).
3. While stream is active, force a credential refresh on the client side (rotate ephemeral token or simulate delegated credential expiry + refresh mid-stream).
4. Allow the SDK to reconnect/resume the stream. Observe the webhook logs for duplicate invocations correlated with the same conversation id but different request IDs.
5. Collect API gateway request traces and headers for the chunk before and after refresh.
logs: 2026-03-13T15:12:37Z webhook invocation id=wh-001 conversation=conv-77 trigger=func_execute payload_id=pl-77
2026-03-13T15:12:38Z webhook invocation id=wh-002 conversation=conv-77 trigger=func_execute payload_id=pl-77
investigation_notes: Initial triage: header value appears truncated/byte-altered after the gateway processes the token refresh. The base64 suffix changed length and server-side dedupe key no longer matched previous in-flight confirmation record.
Observed the API gateway performing header reconstitution when client presented a rotated auth token; header name preserved but value modified (line-wrapping/truncation in internal proxy).
Python SDK attaches idempotency confirmation as an HTTP header on the streaming chunks. If header is rewritten, server treats resumed chunk as new and re-issues tool call.
Customer's Go webhook is idempotent-by-body but relies on the Redwood confirmation header to avoid executing twice; without consistent header, dedupe fails.

Reproduced in our staging with a simulated credential rotation through the same proxy chain; confirmed header length and line-splitting behaviour under certain chunk-size boundaries (proxy config: max-header-size=8192, chunk-rewrite enabled).
Correlation IDs: api-trace:trace-20260313-abc123. Relevant gateway config: edge-proxy v2.18 with http2->http1 translation enabled on the dedicated stack for QueryFlow.
workaround: Short-term: ask customer to include a per-call idempotency token in the function call payload (body) instead of relying solely on headers. Alternatively, disable mid-stream auth rotation on their delegated token (increase TTL) while long streams are active. We can also ask them to patch webhook to dedupe using body payload_id.
resolution: In progress: engineering to patch two places — (1) edge proxy config to preserve header values across auth refreshes and avoid any line-wrapping/truncation; (2) server-side fallback to accept idempotency confirmation that arrives in the body if header is missing (opt-in via 'idempotency_fallback' flag). Patch PR created against edge-proxy and streaming-service. Temporary mitigation guidance provided to customer (see comments).
comments: 2026-03-13 16:05 - Support (Ava Thompson): Collected initial reproducer from customer, requested gateway logs and webhook request IDs. Customer confirmed duplicates happened ~3 times in last 24h. Asked them to run test harness with increased token TTL.

2026-03-13 18:22 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Reproduced locally with dedicated stack config. Found header line-splitting at 8k boundary when token refresh happens concurrently with chunk flush. Filed infra bug and started edge-proxy change. Assigned to Diego for patching.

2026-03-14 09:12 - Engineering (Priya Nair): Created PR to add body-based idempotency fallback. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-service/pull/3290. Needs review from security (to ensure fallback doesn't open replay attacks).

2026-03-14 11:30 - Support (Ava Thompson): Provided customer workaround steps: (1) add 'client_idempotency_key' to funcall payload; (2) increase ephemeral token TTL during long sessions; (3) update webhook dedupe by payload_id. Customer confirmed they can apply (1) immediately.
2026-03-14 14:00 - Security (Liam O'Connor): Raised concern about accepting idempotency in body without HMAC. Suggested adding signed idempotency tokens in future patch.
